claim: Olaparib improves progression-free survival in BRCA-mutated advanced ovarian cancer
gold_rationale: Overwhelming, consistent Level-1 evidence with regulatory endorsement. The pivotal double-blind phase 3 SOLO-1 trial (Moore, NEJM 2018; NCT01844986) enrolled exactly the claimed population — newly-diagnosed BRCA1/2-mutated advanced (FIGO III-IV) high-grade ovarian cancer in response to first-line platinum chemotherapy — with the CLAIMED outcome (investigator-assessed PFS) as its PRIMARY endpoint. It met that endpoint decisively: 70% reduction in risk of progression or death (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.23-0.41, p<0.001). The 5-year post-hoc PFS update (Banerjee, Lancet Oncol 2021) confirmed durability: median PFS 56.0 vs 13.8 months (HR 0.33). The 7-year OS analysis (DiSilvestro, JCO) showed a clinically meaningful survival benefit (HR 0.55; 67.0% vs 46.5% alive at 7 years), reinforcing that the PFS gain translated downstream even though the prespecified ultra-stringent OS significance threshold (p<0.0001) was not formally crossed (observed p=0.0004). PAOLA-1 (Ray-Coquard, NEJM 2019) independently confirmed a PFS benefit of olaparib (added to bevacizumab) with a large PFS gain in the BRCAm/HRD subgroups. The FDA (Dec 19, 2018) approved olaparib as first-line maintenance in this population on the strength of SOLO-1 PFS, the first PARP inhibitor so approved, and it is a guideline standard of care. No credible contradicting trial exists. Consensus: Supported.
population: newly-diagnosed BRCA-mutated advanced (FIGO III-IV) ovarian cancer in complete/partial response after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy
provenance: PubMed (all four PMIDs independently re-verified: titles/journals/volumes/pages/DOIs match, none retracted), ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01844986 full record confirms Phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled design with investigator-assessed PFS as PRIMARY endpoint and OS as SECONDARY), and FDA drug-approval record (Dec 19, 2018, verified via fda.gov + AstraZeneca/Merck/ASCO Post).
notes: Evidence base is uniformly and strongly supportive; no contradicting RCT identified. Nuance for gate logic: SOLO-1's PRIMARY endpoint IS the claimed outcome (PFS) — not a surrogate for the claim — so outcome_match=true across PFS rows. The 7-year OS row (secondary endpoint) is directionally supportive (HR 0.55) but did not formally meet the prespecified p<0.0001 bar (observed p=0.0004); relative to the PFS claim it is a non-primary/surrogate endpoint, so outcome_match=false. PAOLA-1 population is broader (all-comers on bevacizumab regardless of BRCA/HRD status) so population_match=false for that row, though its BRCAm/HRD subgroup effect is concordant. Adversarial fact-check fix: row 5 source_id was a fabricated DOI, replaced with the real FDA URL.

rows.citation: Moore K, Colombo N, Scambia G, et al. Maintenance Olaparib in Patients with Newly Diagnosed Advanced Ovarian Cancer. N Engl J Med. 2018;379(26):2495-2505. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1810858
rows.integrity_note: Verified: PMID resolves to this exact article (title/journal/vol 379(26)/pp 2495-2505/DOI all match); not retracted. Pivotal double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3 RCT (NCT01844986); PFS is the PRIMARY endpoint and equals the claimed outcome. AstraZeneca/Merck funded; results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov (has_results=true).
rows.finding: In newly-diagnosed BRCA1/2-mutated advanced ovarian cancer in response to platinum chemotherapy, olaparib maintenance reduced risk of progression or death by 70% vs placebo (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.23-0.41, p<0.001); 3-yr freedom from progression 60% vs 27% (n=260 olaparib/131 placebo). Directly supports the claim.

rows.citation: Banerjee S, Moore KN, Colombo N, et al. Maintenance olaparib for newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer and a BRCA mutation (SOLO1/GOG 3004): 5-year follow-up. Lancet Oncol. 2021;22(12):1721-1731. DOI:10.1016/S1470-2045(21)00531-3
rows.integrity_note: Verified: PMID resolves to this exact article (title/journal Lancet Oncol/vol 22(12)/pp 1721-1731/DOI all match); not retracted. Post-hoc 5-year PFS update of the same pivotal SOLO-1 RCT (NCT01844986); PFS remains the outcome of interest. Abstract confirms n=260 olaparib/131 placebo, data cutoff March 5 2020, post-hoc analysis.
rows.finding: At 5-year follow-up (post-hoc), median PFS was 56.0 months (95% CI 41.9-NR) with olaparib vs 13.8 months (11.1-18.2) with placebo (HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.25-0.43). Confirms durable PFS benefit sustained beyond the 2-year treatment period.

rows.citation: DiSilvestro P, Banerjee S, Colombo N, et al. Overall Survival With Maintenance Olaparib at a 7-Year Follow-Up in Newly Diagnosed Advanced Ovarian Cancer and a BRCA Mutation: SOLO1/GOG 3004. J Clin Oncol. 2023;41(3):609-617. DOI:10.1200/JCO.22.01549
rows.integrity_note: Verified: PMID resolves to this exact article (title/journal JCO/vol 41(3)/pp 609-617/DOI all match); not retracted (PubMed online date 2022-09-09; JCO issue 2023). Same pivotal SOLO-1 RCT; the reported endpoint is OVERALL SURVIVAL (a prespecified SECONDARY endpoint), NOT the claimed PFS outcome — so outcome_match=false relative to the PFS claim. Abstract confirms HR 0.55 (0.40-0.76), p=0.0004 with <0.0001 required to declare significance. Directionally corroborative.
rows.finding: At 7-year follow-up, OS HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.40-0.76; p=0.0004, <0.0001 required for significance); 67.0% (olaparib) vs 46.5% (placebo) alive at 7 years. Corroborates that the PFS benefit translates into meaningful long-term survival, though the prespecified OS significance threshold was not formally met.

rows.citation: Ray-Coquard I, Pautier P, Pignata S, et al. Olaparib plus Bevacizumab as First-Line Maintenance in Ovarian Cancer (PAOLA-1/ENGOT-ov25). N Engl J Med. 2019;381(25):2416-2428. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1911361
rows.integrity_note: Verified: PMID resolves to this exact article (title/journal NEJM/vol 381(25)/pp 2416-2428/DOI all match); not retracted. Phase 3 double-blind RCT with investigator-assessed PFS (time to progression/death) as PRIMARY endpoint (outcome_match=true). Abstract confirms population is broader — newly-diagnosed advanced HGOC eligible regardless of BRCA/HRD status, all on bevacizumab backbone — so population_match=false vs the BRCAm-specific claim; BRCAm/HRD subgroup effect is strongly concordant. Registered NCT02477644.
rows.finding: Olaparib+bevacizumab improved PFS vs placebo+bevacizumab (median 22.1 vs 16.6 mo overall; HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.49-0.72, p<0.001; n=537 olaparib/269 placebo), with much larger benefit in HRD-positive subgroups including BRCAm (HR 0.33). Independently confirms olaparib's PFS benefit, including in the BRCAm population.

rows.citation: U.S. FDA. FDA approved olaparib (LYNPARZA, AstraZeneca) for maintenance treatment of BRCA-mutated advanced ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer in complete/partial response to first-line platinum-based chemotherapy. December 19, 2018 (based on SOLO-1, NCT01844986).
rows.integrity_note: Regulatory action, not a trial. Adversarial fix: original corpus source_id 'DOI:10.31525/fda2-ucm627789.htm' was a fabricated/non-resolvable DOI — replaced with the real FDA drug-approval URL. Verified via fda.gov, Merck, AstraZeneca, and ASCO Post: approval date Dec 19, 2018; first PARP-inhibitor first-line maintenance approval; granted on the basis of SOLO-1 PFS (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.23-0.41, p<0.0001) in the claimed population.
rows.finding: FDA approved olaparib first-line maintenance for germline/somatic BRCA-mutated advanced ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer in complete/partial response to platinum chemotherapy, citing SOLO-1 PFS (70% reduction in progression/death, HR 0.30). Establishes regulatory consensus that olaparib improves PFS in this population.

baseline.text: Yes. Olaparib significantly improves progression-free survival in patients with BRCA-mutated advanced ovarian cancer. This is best established by the phase 3 SOLO-1 trial (Moore et al., NEJM 2018), which studied olaparib maintenance in newly-diagnosed BRCA1/2-mutated advanced ovarian cancer patients in response to first-line platinum chemotherapy. Olaparib reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 70% versus placebo (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.23-0.41, p<0.001), and longer follow-up showed median PFS of 56 months with olaparib versus about 14 months with placebo. On the basis of SOLO-1, the FDA approved olaparib as first-line maintenance therapy in this population in December 2018, and it is a guideline-endorsed standard of care.
